000
FXUS61 KPHI 271113
AFDPHI

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Mount Holly NJ
713 AM EDT Thu Aug 27 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Flood Watch expanded to include the Lehigh Valley and Berks 
County.

Updated the aviation section for the 06Z TAFs.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1. A warm front on Thursday will bring the next chance for 
widespread rain.

2. A cold front is expected to follow close behind on Friday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...A warm front tomorrow will bring the next 
chance for widespread rain. 

Early morning convection has not been initialized well by the
CAMs with many of the 06Z guidance missing it entirely.
Ironically, the previous 00Z and 18Z guidance hi res runs
displayed the morning convection a bit earlier. Right now, the
greatest threat from these storms looks to be localized flash
flooding, but a severe thunderstorm cannot be fully ruled out.

High pressure moves offshore with southerly return flow behind 
a warm front will bring dew points into the low 70s. Showers and 
thunderstorms will start moving into western areas before 
daybreak and continue through the day. CAMS producing some 
organization to convective activity largely focused on the I-95 
urban corridor. 

As for the hazards, there is a SLIGHT (2 out of 4) risk for 
excessive rainfall. Precipitable water values increase to 
perhaps as high as 150% of normal for this time of year. 
The hires guidance suggests that heaviest precipitation will be
generally along the I-95 corridor and points northwest. Hires
guidance has also pointed to areas along the I-78 corridor
potentially seeing heavy rainfall amounts as well. Generally 
around 1-2 inches of rain with localized QPF values in excess of
3 inches. Widespread flash flooding still seems unlikely, but 
the localized threat remains elevated. The Flood Watch was 
expanded to include the Lehigh Valley and Berks county and
remains in effect for northern NJ and the I-95 corridor.

For severe hazards, latest CAMS and HREF guidance show SBCAPE
values remaining around 1500-2500 J/kg with ensemble maximums 
in excess 3000 J/kg. Deep layer shear forecasts remain around 
30kt with a strongly veering profile aloft. Boundary layer flow
is not particularly strong but surface winds are more backed 
than previous forecasts so an isolated tornado is possible 
primarily along and west of I-95. That said, damaging wind gusts 
and hail will remain the greatest threat. Dominant mode should 
be multicell convection but a supercell can't be ruled out 
especially where cloud bearing shear is maximized. SPC has 
expanded the area of a slight risk (2 out of 5) to now include 
much of the area. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...A cold front will cross the area Friday.

The timing of this cold front will be critical in the risk for 
thunderstorm hazards. There are differences between models in 
both the timing, and if this will be a single cold front, or an 
initial cold front with a reinforcing shot of cold air advection
coming in behind it. Saturday and Sunday appear to be dry across
most of the area with the exception of southern areas Saturday
where low probabilities of showers and storms will exist.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
The following discussion is for KPHL, KPNE, KTTN, KABE, KRDG, 
KILG, KMIV, KACY and surrounding areas.

Thursday...Mainly VFR. Light south winds in the morning become 
more out of the south-southwest at around 10 knots during the 
afternoon with gusts to 20 knots for KMIV/KACY. For the Lehigh
Valley and I-95 terminals, showers and potentially an embedded
thunderstorm are possible in the morning which was handled with
VCSH with a PROB30 for -TSRA. As the potential for showers and 
thunderstorms increases from midday into the evening, VCTS and 
PROB30 groups for TSRA for most terminals to account for this 
activity. 

Thursday night...VFR as showers and storms exit, but patchy fog
possible mainly across the I-95 corridor and RDG/ABE. Winds
light and variable. Low confidence.

Outlook...

Friday...Periods of MVFR or lower are possible in showers and
storms.

Saturday through Monday...Prevailing VFR conditions.

&&

.MARINE...
No marine hazards expected. Southerly winds with gusts near 20 
kt possible.

Outlook...

Thursday night and through Sunday...No marine hazards expected.

Rip Currents...

On Thursday, winds remain southerly at 10 to 15 mph with gusts 
to 20 to 25 mph. There is an east-southeasterly swell with a 
period of 8-9 seconds and breaking waves around 2-3 feet. As a 
result, there is a MODERATE risk for the development of 
dangerous and life threatening rip currents at the Jersey Shore 
and a LOW risk at Delaware Beaches.

For Friday, winds in the morning are more westerly at 5 to 10 
mph before becoming more southwesterly in the afternoon at 5 to
10 mph. An east-southeasterly swell remains with a period of 
6-7 seconds with breaking waves around 2-3 feet. As a result, 
there is a MODERATE risk for the development of dangerous and 
life threatening rip currents at the Jersey Shore and a LOW risk
at Delaware Beaches.

For specific beach forecasts, visit weather.gov/beach/phi

&&

.PHI WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
PA...Flood Watch from noon EDT today through late tonight for 
     PAZ060>062-070-071-101>106.
NJ...Flood Watch from noon EDT today through late tonight for 
     NJZ001-007>010-012-013-015-017>019.
DE...Flood Watch from noon EDT today through late tonight for 
     DEZ001.
MD...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...WFO PHI
AVIATION...WFO PHI
MARINE...WFO PHI
